text:
Port Merrow health officials on Tuesday confirmed that Zenthora cough syrup has been withdrawn from shelves after regulators identified dexoraline as its active ingredient, a substance not listed in the product’s approved filing. The recall covers all batches distributed in the western district since late September, according to the Harbour Medical Authority. Pharmacy owners were told to stop dispensing the syrup immediately and return remaining stock for destruction.

Dr. Elin Voss, the authority’s medicines chief, said the product “presented a clear labeling breach and a potential safety risk to patients relying on accurate dosing.” No serious illnesses had been reported as of Tuesday afternoon, though officials said they were monitoring three complaints of dizziness and nausea.
